statement: A cubic $f(x)=x^{3}+ax^{2}+bx+c$ satisfies $f(1)=5$, $f(-1)=-1$, $f(2)=17$ and $f(-2)=-7$. Find $a$, $b$ and $c$.
solution: From the values: $1+a+b+c=5\\Rightarrow a+b+c=4$; $-1+a-b+c=-1\\Rightarrow a-b+c=0$; $8+4a+2b+c=17\\Rightarrow 4a+2b+c=9$; $-8+4a-2b+c=-7\\Rightarrow 4a-2b+c=1$. Subtracting the second from the first gives $2b=4$ so $b=2$; then $a+c=2$, and $4a+c=5$, whence $a=1$, $c=1$. Thus $a=1,b=2,c=1$.
hints: Use the remainder theorem to get four linear equations.
Subtract pairs to isolate $b$, then $a$ and $c$.
